faq.q: What source photo works for a drink clip?
faq.a: Use a sharp photo of the full bottle or can with its shape, cap and visible label area clear.

faq.q: Can the video show a pour?
faq.a: Yes. Choose a serving scene with a glass, ice or garnish and keep the package visible beside the action.

faq.q: Can the clip show ice and condensation?
faq.a: Yes. A cold drink scene can include ice, bubbles or condensation. Keep claims about flavor and ingredients in your verified listing.

faq.q: What length fits a pour clip?
faq.a: Use 6 seconds for one pour or opening, 10 or 15 seconds for a tasting beat, and 30 seconds for several serving moments.

faq.q: Where do flavor and allergen details go?
faq.a: Add the verified flavor, ingredients and allergen information as text in your editor or product listing after download.

faq.q: Do I need a studio or a creator?
faq.a: No. The clip is generated from your bottle or can photo, so you can prepare a serving scene without booking a kitchen shoot.

visual.overview: Build the ad around one clear serving action. Keep the package recognizable while a pour, first sip or simple preparation gives viewers something concrete to watch.

steps.prompt: Use the uploaded photo as the product and preserve its shape, color and visible label area exactly. A hand pours citrus soda from the silver can into one ice-filled tumbler.
